activation_gate.gate: The principal's interim intent-signing ruling LANDED on 2026-11-16 (23:52 CST), negative: 'Intent signing should not be a lesser act at this time.' Intent signing is custody-grade, identical in grade to custody signing; there is no lesser policy-key path for negotiation. Activation of live negotiation therefore requires the production SKAP custody signing path to be settled — negotiation waits on that path, not on a further ruling. Until that path is settled, the endpoint build proceeds but no live negotiation or signing occurs. UPDATE 2026-11-17 (BUILD-Q-14): the production SKAP custody signing path is SETTLED and signing is live via the sign-under-seal operation; crossings settle via the endpoint's own gas-only relayer (Gate 2). The gated state described in this paragraph is historical.
activation_gate.negotiating_identity: The negotiating identity is a dedicated identity specifically for the machine economy, distinct from the suite-side identity — identities are per profit center (the principal's determination, 2026-11-16). Its designation landed on 2026-11-16 (23:56–23:57 CST): the operative designation is the digits 8374 — the digits represent BETA (8=B, 3=E, 7=T, 4=A) as meaning/expansion, and identity form follows the economy (digits for the machine economy; letters for the suite economy). Designation only: the identity does not yet exist as a declared receptor — formal namespace registration is a separate governed act at gated activation, and it is not asserted as a declared receptor in this offer. UPDATE 2026-11-17 (BUILD-Q-17): the identity is registered as 8374@StegVerse.ai and the receptor is declared under tonight's operating configuration.
activation_gate.not_gated: Endpoint build and offer publication do not wait on the custody signing path.
activation_gate.revisability: The ruling is landed as CURRENT POSTURE ('at this time'): changeable policy, capable of being changed in the near future if the market sees things differently, supersedeable only by a later principal determination — which would arrive as a new generation of this suite. It is not an invariant of the endpoint's design.

offered_resources.description: Admissibility evaluation of a machine-proposed transaction or action at the signing boundary, under the ecosystem disposition grammar (ALLOW / DENY / FAIL_CLOSED). Only ALLOW commits, at the signing boundary this service controls; execution paths that do not pass through this endpoint's evaluation are outside that boundary.

Issuance of a dual-recorded receipt pair for a governed crossing: receipts attach to transitions, not transactions, and one boundary crossing yields one matched pair — two records, one per side of the crossing, hash-chained — constituting a portable settlement proof: the pair is verifiable by either side against the chain's anchors without trusting the other party's internal log. Independent retention of the pair by the customer is not yet demonstrated; it is the subject of BUILD-Q-44. A refused or fail-closed attempt likewise produces a receipt: the refusal record.

Agreement receipting under the admitted scope ME-AGREE-01 (BUILD-Q-49, admitted 2026-11-18): a bot or agent that has reached an agreement — deal terms accepted by both sides — records it as a governed crossing with action "record-agreement" before treating the deal as final. The crossing carries the commit-time evidence object (authority, delegation, evidence_refs, exclusions, policy ME-POLICY-01, validity_at_commit) and the resource names the agreement being receipted (form: agreement-record:<agreement reference>). On ALLOW the crossing issues the matched receipt pair for the agreement; on NON-ALLOW the attempt is refused or fails closed with the six-field disposition and a refusal receipt, and the fee position follows the offer's active pricing mode. Priced at the full-evaluation tier: the governance fee (15,000 micro-USDC) plus the settlement charge quoted at challenge time (BUILD-Q-43 / offer v07); the challenge amount is the total authorized.

fee_position.position: The fee is a posted, non-negotiable toll — 'The fee is the fee' (principal, 2026-11-16 23:52 CST). Negotiation in the machine economy concerns the work and the terms of the crossing, never the governance fee.
fee_position.pricing_mode_status: The mode (a)/(b) structure in pricing.pricing_mode stands as STANDING pricing structure, set as policy — expressly not per-transaction bargaining.
fee_position.revisability: This fee position and the intent-signing ruling (activation_gate) are landed as CURRENT POSTURE, capable of being changed in the near future if the market sees things differently; either is supersedeable only by a later principal determination, which would arrive as a new generation of this suite. Neither is an invariant of the endpoint's design.

modes.description: The fee is charged per evaluation regardless of outcome: an ALLOW, a DENY, and a FAIL_CLOSED each bear the fee for the unit of compute they consumed. This is the ACTIVE mode under the current operating configuration.

The ALLOW disposition price covers all dispositions: the cost of refused evaluations is amortized into the ALLOW price; a refusal draws no separate charge, and its compute is paid for through the ALLOW price. This mode is NOT active.

pricing_mode.refusal_compute: Refusal compute is fee-bearing under either mode: a NON-ALLOW attempt consumes exactly one unit of compute (1 receipt pair, ALLOW or NON-ALLOW), and that unit is paid for under mode (a) directly or under mode (b) through the ALLOW price.
pricing_mode.selection: The pricing structure is a selectable cost-optimization option for the consumer of the service; the mode changes the shape of the charge, never whether the compute is paid. The selected mode is standing pricing structure set as policy; it is not negotiated per transaction, and the fee itself is never a subject of negotiation (see pricing.fee_position).

settlement_charge.applies_to: every paid crossing, both tiers, under the active pricing mode
settlement_charge.determination: Principal determination 2026-11-18 (BUILD-Q-43): the ratified tiers are WITHOUT settlement gas; settlement gas is an additional fee charged on the crossing, never absorbed by StegVerse. Rationale stated by the principal: absorbing volatile gas could bankrupt StegVerse during gas-price spikes.
settlement_charge.computation: settlement charge = gas_units_basis x max_fee_per_gas x ETH/USD, quoted at challenge time and rounded up to the next micro-USDC. gas_units_basis = 86,679 units (the settlement leg's receipted eth_estimateGas for one transferWithAuthorization settlement of Base USDC, PAIR-000024/PAIR-000034 records); max_fee_per_gas = 2 x pending baseFeePerGas + priority fee, read live via eth_feeHistory / eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas over the endpoint's egress proxy -- the same fee basis the gas-only relayer provisions with; ETH/USD read live (Coinbase spot) over the same proxy.
settlement_charge.total_authorized: the total a payer authorizes = governance fee + settlement charge, stated exactly in each 402 challenge (the v1 body's maxAmountRequired and the v2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED accepts amount agree); verification accepts exactly the quoted total for that crossing
settlement_charge.fail_closed: if a live gas or ETH/USD read fails, no paid challenge is issued (SETTLEMENT_CHARGE_QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE) rather than the charge being silently absorbed

protocol.alternate_dialect: MPP (noted as alternate; x402 is the primary dialect of this offer)
protocol.flow_summary: Machine client requests the governed resource -> endpoint evaluates admissibility at the signing boundary -> on ALLOW the client completes payment authorization under x402 and execution proceeds -> one dual-recorded, hash-chained matched receipt pair issues for the crossing (two records, one per side) as the crossing's settlement proof, verifiable by either side against the chain's anchors. On DENY or FAIL_CLOSED no execution occurs and nothing moves; the response carries the six-field disposition (failure_code, failed_predicate, required_evidence_or_repair, retry_entrypoint, owning goal, next_attempt), and the refused attempt itself produces a receipt — the refusal record — as in the W-1 run (2026-11-13), whose out-of-scope and post-dissolution attempts produced refusal receipts while moving nothing.

terms.compute_unit: Metering counts receipt pairs: 1 receipt pair is a unit of compute, ALLOW or NON-ALLOW (compute-assignment SLOT A, landed by the principal 2026-11-16). An ALLOW crossing's matched pair and a NON-ALLOW attempt's refusal record pair each constitute exactly one unit; the unit is disposition-independent.
terms.dispositions: Every evaluation resolves to ALLOW, DENY, or FAIL_CLOSED. Only ALLOW commits, at the signing boundary this service controls. A non-ALLOW response carries failure_code, failed_predicate, required_evidence_or_repair, retry_entrypoint, owning goal, and next_attempt — a label-only reason is never returned — and the refused or fail-closed attempt produces a receipt (the refusal record) while moving nothing.
terms.fail_closed: Missing evidence, stale authority, or an unevaluable predicate fails the crossing closed; the refused attempt produces a refusal receipt, and reconstruction after the fact supports investigation and never retroactively creates commit-time admissibility.
terms.fees: The fee is paid either way, under a selectable pricing mode: (a) the fee follows all dispositions, or (b) the ALLOW disposition price covers all dispositions. The fee is a posted, non-negotiable toll — negotiation concerns the work and the terms of the crossing, never the governance fee. See pricing.pricing_mode and pricing.fee_position. Settlement gas is not included in the governance fee: it is charged additionally on each crossing, quoted at challenge time from live Base gas conditions and the live ETH/USD rate (principal determination, 2026-11-18, BUILD-Q-43; see pricing.settlement_charge).
terms.no_credentials: This offer holds no credentials and requests none; any signing capability operates under the principal's own custody doctrine (SKAP), never as a stored key in this service.
terms.posture_revisability: The fee position (pricing.fee_position) and the intent-signing ruling (activation_gate) are CURRENT POSTURE: capable of being changed in the near future if the market sees things differently, supersedeable only by a later principal determination arriving as a new generation of this suite. Neither is an invariant of the endpoint's design.
terms.receipts: Receipts attach to transitions, not transactions: each governed crossing produces one dual-recorded, hash-chained matched pair (two records, one per side); the pair — verifiable by either side against the chain's anchors, not dependent on either party's internal log — is the record of the crossing. Independent retention of the pair by the customer is not yet demonstrated (BUILD-Q-44). A refused or fail-closed attempt also produces a receipt — the refusal record — while moving nothing.
